# List of World Series champions
The World Series is the annual championship series of Major League Baseball (MLB) and concludes the MLB postseason. First played in 1903,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_World_Series_champions#cite_note-brefpostseason-1) the World Series championship is a best-of-seven playoff and is a contest between the champions of baseball's National League (NL) and American League (AL).[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_World_Series_champions#cite_note-mlboverview-2) Often referred to as the "Fall Classic",[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_World_Series_champions#cite_note-WShistory-3) the modern World Series has been played every year since 1903 with two exceptions: in 1904, when the NL champion New York Giants declined to play the AL champion Boston Americans; and in 1994, when the series was canceled due to the players' strike.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_World_Series_champions#cite_note-brefpostseason-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_World_Series_champions#cite_note-mlboverview-2)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_World_Series_champions#cite_note-tsn1904-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_World_Series_champions#cite_note-94strike-5) The best-of-seven style has been the format of all World Series except in 1903, 1919, 1920, and 1921, when the winner was determined through a best-of-nine playoff.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_World_Series_champions#cite_note-brefpostseason-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_World_Series_champions#cite_note-mlboverview-2) Although the large majority of contests have been played entirely during the month of October, a small number of Series have also had games played during September and November.

# List of World Series champions
Since 1967, the winning team has been awarded the [Commissioner's Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commissioner's_Trophy_(MLB) "Commissioner's Trophy (MLB)").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_World_Series_champions#cite_note-prnews-6) Players, coaches and others associated with the team are generally given World Series rings to commemorate their victory; however, they have received other items such as pocket watches and medallions in the past.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_World_Series_champions#cite_note-7)

# List of World Series champions
A total of 122 World Series have been contested through 2026, with the AL champion winning 68 and the NL champion winning 54. The New York Yankees of the AL have played in 41 World Series, winning 27 – the most championship appearances and most victories by any MLB team. The Los Angeles Dodgers and the Yankees are tied for the most losses with 14 each. The St. Louis Cardinals have won 11 championships, the most among NL clubs and second-most all-time behind the Yankees.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_World_Series_champions#cite_note-WShistory-3) The Dodgers have represented the NL the most in the World Series with 23 appearances. The Seattle Mariners are the only MLB franchise that has never appeared in a World Series; the San Diego Padres, Tampa Bay Rays, and Colorado Rockies have all played in the Series but have never won it, with the Padres appearing twice, and Rays appearing three times. The Los Angeles Angels and Washington Nationals won their only World Series appearance, and the Miami Marlins are the only team with multiple World Series appearances and no losses with two. The Toronto Blue Jays are the only franchise from outside the United States to appear in and win a World Series, winning in 1992 and 1993. The Houston Astros and Milwaukee Brewers have represented both the NL and AL in the World Series, with the Astros playing in 2005 for the NL and four times (2017, 2019, 2021, 2022) for the AL, while the Brewers played in 1982 for the AL and 2026 for the NL. The 1919 and 2017 World Series were both marred with cheating scandals: the Black Sox Scandal and the Houston Astros sign stealing scandal. The most recent World Series champions are the Milwaukee Brewers.
The last team to repeat as champions was the Dodgers in 2025. Two World Series matchups (in 1982 and 2005) have no current possibility of a rematch due to one of the contending teams switching to the opposing league – the Milwaukee Brewers moved to the NL in 1998, and the Houston Astros moved to the AL in 2013.

# List of World Series champions
The World Series is the annual championship series of Major League Baseball (MLB) and concludes the MLB postseason. First played in 1903,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_World_Series_champions#cite_note-brefpostseason-1) the World Series championship is a best-of-seven playoff and is a contest between the champions of baseball's National League (NL) and American League (AL).[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_World_Series_champions#cite_note-mlboverview-2) Often referred to as the "Fall Classic",[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_World_Series_champions#cite_note-WShistory-3) the modern World Series has been played every year since 1903 with two exceptions: in 1904, when the NL champion New York Giants declined to play the AL champion Boston Americans; and in 1994, when the series was canceled due to the players' strike.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_World_Series_champions#cite_note-brefpostseason-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_World_Series_champions#cite_note-mlboverview-2)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_World_Series_champions#cite_note-tsn1904-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_World_Series_champions#cite_note-94strike-5) The best-of-seven style has been the format of all World Series except in 1903, 1919, 1920, and 1921, when the winner was determined through a best-of-nine playoff.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_World_Series_champions#cite_note-brefpostseason-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_World_Series_champions#cite_note-mlboverview-2) Although the large majority of contests have been played entirely during the month of October, a small number of Series have also had games played during September and November.

Since 1967, the winning team has been awarded the [Commissioner's Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commissioner's_Trophy_(MLB) "Commissioner's Trophy (MLB)").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_World_Series_champions#cite_note-prnews-6) Players, coaches and others associated with the team are generally given World Series rings to commemorate their victory; however, they have received other items such as pocket watches and medallions in the past.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_World_Series_champions#cite_note-7)

# List of World Series champions
A total of 122 World Series have been contested through 2026, with the AL champion winning 68 and the NL champion winning 54. The New York Yankees of the AL have played in 41 World Series, winning 27 – the most championship appearances and most victories by any MLB team. The Los Angeles Dodgers and the Yankees are tied for the most losses with 14 each. The St. Louis Cardinals have won 11 championships, the most among NL clubs and second-most all-time behind the Yankees.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_World_Series_champions#cite_note-WShistory-3) The Dodgers have represented the NL the most in the World Series with 23 appearances. The Seattle Mariners are the only MLB franchise that has never appeared in a World Series; the San Diego Padres, Tampa Bay Rays, and Colorado Rockies have all played in the Series but have never won it, with the Padres appearing twice, and Rays appearing three times. The Los Angeles Angels and Washington Nationals won their only World Series appearance, and the Miami Marlins are the only team with multiple World Series appearances and no losses with two. The Toronto Blue Jays are the only franchise from outside the United States to appear in and win a World Series, winning in 1992 and 1993. The Houston Astros and Milwaukee Brewers have represented both the NL and AL in the World Series, with the Astros playing in 2005 for the NL and four times (2017, 2019, 2021, 2022) for the AL, while the Brewers played in 1982 for the AL and 2026 for the NL. The 1919 and 2017 World Series were both marred with cheating scandals: the Black Sox Scandal and the Houston Astros sign stealing scandal. The most recent World Series champions are the Milwaukee Brewers.
The last team to repeat as champions was the Dodgers in 2025. Two World Series matchups (in 1982 and 2005) have no current possibility of a rematch due to one of the contending teams switching to the opposing league – the Milwaukee Brewers moved to the NL in 1998, and the Houston Astros moved to the AL in 2013.

# List of World Series champions
The World Series is the annual championship series of Major League Baseball (MLB) and concludes the MLB postseason. First played in 1903,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_World_Series_champions#cite_note-brefpostseason-1) the World Series championship is a best-of-seven playoff and is a contest between the champions of baseball's National League (NL) and American League (AL).[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_World_Series_champions#cite_note-mlboverview-2) Often referred to as the "Fall Classic",[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_World_Series_champions#cite_note-WShistory-3) the modern World Series has been played every year since 1903 with two exceptions: in 1904, when the NL champion New York Giants declined to play the AL champion Boston Americans; and in 1994, when the series was canceled due to the players' strike.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_World_Series_champions#cite_note-brefpostseason-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_World_Series_champions#cite_note-mlboverview-2)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_World_Series_champions#cite_note-tsn1904-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_World_Series_champions#cite_note-94strike-5) The best-of-seven style has been the format of all World Series except in 1903, 1919, 1920, and 1921, when the winner was determined through a best-of-nine playoff.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_World_Series_champions#cite_note-brefpostseason-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_World_Series_champions#cite_note-mlboverview-2) Although the large majority of contests have been played entirely during the month of October, a small number of Series have also had games played during September and November.

# List of World Series champions
Since 1967, the winning team has been awarded the [Commissioner's Trophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commissioner's_Trophy_(MLB) "Commissioner's Trophy (MLB)").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_World_Series_champions#cite_note-prnews-6) Players, coaches and others associated with the team are generally given World Series rings to commemorate their victory; however, they have received other items such as pocket watches and medallions in the past.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_World_Series_champions#cite_note-7)

# List of World Series champions
A total of 122 World Series have been contested through 2026, with the AL champion winning 68 and the NL champion winning 54. The New York Yankees of the AL have played in 41 World Series, winning 27 – the most championship appearances and most victories by any MLB team. The Los Angeles Dodgers and the Yankees are tied for the most losses with 14 each. The St. Louis Cardinals have won 11 championships, the most among NL clubs and second-most all-time behind the Yankees.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_World_Series_champions#cite_note-WShistory-3) The Dodgers have represented the NL the most in the World Series with 23 appearances. The Seattle Mariners are the only MLB franchise that has never appeared in a World Series; the San Diego Padres, Tampa Bay Rays, and Colorado Rockies have all played in the Series but have never won it, with the Padres appearing twice, and Rays appearing three times. The Los Angeles Angels and Washington Nationals won their only World Series appearance, and the Miami Marlins are the only team with multiple World Series appearances and no losses with two. The Toronto Blue Jays are the only franchise from outside the United States to appear in and win a World Series, winning in 1992 and 1993. The Houston Astros and Milwaukee Brewers have represented both the NL and AL in the World Series, with the Astros playing in 2005 for the NL and four times (2017, 2019, 2021, 2022) for the AL, while the Brewers played in 1982 for the AL and 2026 for the NL. The 1919 and 2017 World Series were both marred with cheating scandals: the Black Sox Scandal and the Houston Astros sign stealing scandal. The most recent World Series champions are the Milwaukee Brewers.
The last team to repeat as champions was the Dodgers in 2025. Two World Series matchups (in 1982 and 2005) have no current possibility of a rematch due to one of the contending teams switching to the opposing league – the Milwaukee Brewers moved to the NL in 1998, and the Houston Astros moved to the AL in 2013.

MLB Opening Day has expanded, so now opening week is a better term to describe the game schedule. The action begins with the Yankees vs. Giants game on Wednesday, March 25. MLB Opening Day has expanded, so now opening week is a better term to describe the game schedule. The action begins with the Yankees vs. Giants game on Wednesday, March 25. An MLB.TV subscription is a great way to catch all your favorite teams' out-of-market games live.
